display.title: Simchas Beis Hashoeva, Hoshana Rabbah Night: The Dance That Broke the Decree
display.summary_short: On Hoshana Rabbah night, Rabbi Goldstein teaches that today we serve Hashem with simcha, and tells how a Chassid's dancing saved his sick son in the days of the Tzemach Tzedek.
display.summary_long: Recorded live at a Simchas Beis Hashoeva rally for children on the night of Hoshana Rabbah. Rabbi Goldstein wishes everyone a good and sweet year and explains that tonight's Ushpizin, Dovid HaMelech and the Rebbe Rashab, are both connected to Moshiach. A child character arrives with a Tehillim and a Chumash, ready for the Hoshana Rabbah custom of reading Sefer Devarim and saying Tehillim, and asks whether to say it with tears as in the olden days. Rabbi Goldstein explains that the Rebbe taught our generation to serve Hashem with simcha and bitachon, and tells a story: in the time of the Tzemach Tzedek, a Chassid whose son was gravely ill traveled to Lubavitch and received only 'Hashem should help you'. He spent Hoshana Rabbah crying over Tehillim, then decided to dance with all his might through Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah. Before he left, the Tzemach Tzedek told him that his joy had broken a Heavenly decree and his son would recover. Rabbi Goldstein closes with the Zohar's teaching that Heaven gives according to the joy on our faces, and the Rebbe's call to grab another Jew while dancing and bring Moshiach. The emcee then begins the Twelve Pesukim.
display.lesson: Serve Hashem with simcha and trust; true joy can break even a harsh decree and brings blessing from Above.

date.note: Filename '7th day' and 'tonight the Ushpizin are Dovid HaMelech and the Rebbe Rashab' = night of Hoshana Rabbah; 'the year coming is a leap year' fits 5787, so Sukkos 5786 (evening of 12 Oct 2025).

advisories.note: A young boy is gravely ill and doctors cannot help; he recovers through his father's joy.

sources_cited.note: Before giving from Above, Heaven looks at the joy on a person's face (page reference given on air, partly unclear).
In our generation we serve Hashem with simcha rather than tears; 'grab another Jew' while dancing to bring Moshiach; Shanah Tovah Umesukah includes every blessing.
